_doc: KNOWN-DIVERGENCE ALLOWLIST (SPEC roadmap 8 / task PHASE CI). Mirrors connectrpc/conformance's tracked 'known-failing/known-flaky'. An entry NEUTRALIZES a cell's FAIL/SIM verdict in the FINAL GATE EXIT CODE *only* when it carries BOTH (a) a written `reason` and (b) `go_nondeterminism_evidence` proving Go itself is nondeterministic on the diverging field(s) -- the differing Go run SHAs/values the live oracle measured. An entry WITHOUT evidence is REJECTED by the gate (fail-closed): it can never silently turn a real Rust bug green. Match is by exact `label` OR `argv` OR `family`+`kind`. NOTHING here blanks a Go-stable field; that is detected by the tamper layer, not excused here.

_categories.go-nondeterminism: Go's OWN output varies run-to-run on the diverging field(s); evidence = differing Go run SHAs from the live oracle. These DO neutralize the gate exit code.
_categories.tracked-known-failing: A real, tracked Rust port gap (NOT Go-nondeterminism). These are REPORTED but DO NOT neutralize the gate -- a tracked-known-failing is still a real divergence and keeps the exit nonzero (SPEC: 'nonzero exit on any real divergence'). Listed so triage knows it is already on the board, Connect-style.

go_nondeterminism.label: flag:static/clones--languages:Go[json]@hercules
go_nondeterminism.reason: Go itself is nondeterministic on this cell: the reference clone detector (MinHash/LSH) accumulates pairs iterating Go maps, so the issues/clone-pairs ORDER — and, at the top-N issue-cap boundary, the MEMBERSHIP — shuffles run-to-run. 6 consecutive live-Go runs of the exact cell argv produced 6 different full-output SHAs (2026-08-02: 3c481ea8, c9d86200, 4bf5965e, 688e8bb2, d560c6e6, 020ee80b). The Rust port is deterministic; the numeric clone metrics (counts, ratios, types) agree with Go whenever Go is frozen at one seed.

go_nondeterminism_evidence.observed_distribution: 6 consecutive live-Go runs on 2026-08-02: all 6 full-output SHAs distinct (issues list order + membership at the cap boundary shuffle)
go_nondeterminism_evidence.note: The flakes land in the flag family because --languages narrows the candidate set onto the map-iteration-dominated pairing paths; measured canonicalization cannot normalize ORDER-sensitive top-N membership.

go_nondeterminism.label: static:static/cohesion[text]@ioq3
go_nondeterminism.reason: The reference implementation picks the section Summary message by iterating a Go MAP of numeric averages and using the FIRST value (internal/analyzers/common/aggregator.go: `for _, value := range averages { message = messageBuilder(value); break }`). Go map iteration order is randomized, and on ioq3 the three cohesion averages (lcom=0.7, cohesion_score=0.3, function_cohesion) straddle the message thresholds, so Go's own Summary line flips run-to-run. The numeric metrics are byte-identical between Go and Rust; only the message text diverges when Go happens to pick a different key than Rust's deterministic choice.

Summary: Poor overall cohesion - significant refactoring recommended
go_nondeterminism_evidence.observed_distribution: 8 consecutive live-Go runs on 2026-07-26: 5x Excellent, 3x Poor
go_nondeterminism_evidence.note: The gate's n_go=3 oracle runs happened to agree by chance (p~0.1-0.3 per label mix), which is why measured canonicalization did not normalize this field.

tracked_known_failing.reason: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-02 (was: 'oracle-exceeds-own-budget', unexplained timeout). Covers the 6 --include-vendored@hercules static cells (complexity + halstead across json/text/yaml formats). TWO layers, both diagnosed: (1) The frozen-oracle timeout is a Go BUG, not untestability: pkg/uast/parser_dsl.go toCanonicalNode re-walks every unmapped subtree twice (2^depth blowup); a PERF-ONLY, output-byte-identical patch (oracle/patches/uast-unmapped-subtree-rewalk-perf.patch — the same restructure Rust landed in cf-uast/src/lowering.rs) makes the oracle complete the cell with a full 5351785-byte report (measured 2026-08-02; the patch is proven byte-identical to the frozen binary on 9 diverse static/history cells). (2) With the oracle now completable, the residual divergence is REAL and DELIBERATE on the Rust side: Rust's durabilility caps skip vendor/gopkg.in/vmarkovtsev/BiDiSentiment.v1/assets/bindata.go (70.5MB > the 64MiB read cap; Go has no such cap and parses it), yielding 21473 vs Go's 21494 total functions (the 19 top-level funcs + 2 methods of bindata.go) on complexity, and the corresponding halstead-token/function-count deltas on halstead, plus tie-order diffs in the capped issues list. Cells stay RED: measuring them in-suite needs an oracle re-bless (tamper_check --bless, oracle SHA is fingerprinted) plus a policy call on the deliberate durability caps and a ~20min-per-cell runtime.

tracked_known_failing.label: fuzz:FuzzSerializer*/invalid-utf8-source
tracked_known_failing.reason: Real, tracked port gap on sources containing INVALID UTF-8 bytes: the reference implementation's Go strings carry raw bytes, so byte offsets into a function's token always align with the original source; the Rust port stores tokens as String via from_utf8_lossy, which inflates each invalid sequence into a 3-byte U+FFFD and shifts every later offset. Offset-derived operator/decision-point extraction (cf-complexity FunctionSourceContext / binary_operator_from_offsets) then misreads tokens after the corruption point, e.g. missing a `&&` (cyclomatic 7 vs Go's 8, avg 4.0 vs 4.5) on the distilled find. Valid-UTF-8 sources (i.e. real code) are unaffected. Fixing it means carrying raw bytes through Node.token (bstr-style) and lossy-converting only at serialization boundaries — an architectural change, tracked rather than patched around.
